label: gl-no-depth-buffer, before: the GL window takes SDL's default depth (16 asked, 24 granted) with its 8-bit stencil
kind: real-window GL probe, not a perf-suite capture (the suite never builds the GL surface)
machine: SPELDATOR, i7-14700K, RTX 4080 driver 610.62, Windows 11 26200, HDR display 4K at 150%, 120 Hz
configuration: Release (JIT), HULTUI_A11Y=0, SDL_WINDOW_ACTIVATE_WHEN_SHOWN=0, HULTUI_STARTUP=1, P-cores, idle-gated before every run, before and after alternating ABBA

probes.mem: a GL window (24 rows of text in rounded boxes) opened at 1400x900 layout units, pushed to the bottom of the z-order without activation, read after 2 s (A); then grown to its monitor's work area with SetWindowPos NOACTIVATE, the size a maximized window gets, and read after 2 s (B). GPU memory three ways: the 'GPU Process Memory' Dedicated Usage counter Task Manager shows, DXGI IDXGIAdapter3::QueryVideoMemoryInfo CurrentUsage for the process (local segment), and nvidia-smi memory.used for the whole GPU minus a reading taken before the GL driver loaded. Depth and stencil from SDL_GL_GetAttribute on the window's context.
probes.startupJunction: Junction (JIT Release) on a 13-commit scratch repository, HULTUI_STARTUP=1, closed by JUNCTION_BENCH=close@3000
probes.pixels: a temporary probe (not committed) reading the back buffer before each swap: Junction History and Vesper on fixed scratch content, last frame compared byte for byte; and a scene drawn straight onto the window's own SKSurface over FBO 0 with the framework's GRContext (non-antialiased concave and even-odd fills, non-antialiased complex clips, a translucent self-crossing stroke, text through an oval clip, plus antialiased versions), read back with SKSurface.ReadPixels. Stencil work counted by wrapping glEnable, glClear, glStencilFunc and glStencilFuncSeparate.
